rules.rule: Check for self-harm or suicide risk
rules.problem: Type and trigger right; check_for covers every discriminating question in the box. Minor: 'Planning suicide' appears both Current-qualified (Q2) and unqualified (Q3, meant as 'in past month') with nothing to tell the health worker apart; the past-year window on the two History-of situations is not expressed at the point of asking.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable high risk of self-harm or suicide
rules.problem: and/or structure matches the page (Q2 Yes, or Q3 Yes and Q4 Yes) and probable is right for the box's own conclusion label. Two issues: (1) 'Distress' is far broader than 'distressed' (its descendants include Respiratory distress and Fetal distress), so an unrelated distress finding plus a past-month thought would make the patient high risk; use 'Mental distress'. (2) The Q1 = Yes branch (attempted) flows into the same 'Avoid leaving patient alone / Refer urgently' management as High risk, but neither Suicide attempt nor Intentionally harming self appears in this rule; the page's label box is not on that path, so this is a judgment call, but a patient who has just attempted is left with no risk diagnosis.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable low risk of self-harm or suicide
rules.problem: The due_to is made only of (no ...) conditions with no positive anchor. The page's low-risk patient is one who has 'considered self-harm or suicide' (entered the box) and answered No to Q1 and Q2 and either No to Q3 or No to Q4. As written the rule either fires for every patient with nothing recorded (labelling everyone 'At low risk for suicide') or never fires because nothing recorded matches it. It also drops the Q3 = No branch: on the page a patient with no recent thoughts/acts is low risk regardless of agitation/violence/distress, but the rule demands absence of all four. Fix: anchor with (or Thoughts of self harm, History of attempted suicide, History of deliberate self harm) and keep the negations; ideally (and anchor (no Q1) (no Q2) (or (no Q3-window) (no Q4))) if negated onset windows are expressible.

Urgent is justified by the box heading 'Give urgent attention to the patient who has attempted/considered self-harm or suicide'. Note two judgment calls: 'Thoughts of self harm' unqualified makes the page's low-risk patient ('Manage below') Urgent as well, which follows the heading literally but not the page's outcome; and the attempted branch routes through airway/breathing/circulation (page 18), so a higher level for Suicide attempt / Intentionally harming self could be argued.

summary: The low-risk diagnosis rule has no positive anchor (only 'no' conditions) and omits the page's Q3 = No branch, so it will either tag every patient as 'At low risk for suicide' or never fire; it needs an anchor such as Thoughts of self harm or a History-of situation. 'Distress' is used where the page means emotional distress, and its SNOMED descendants include respiratory and fetal distress, which would wrongly push patients to high risk (fix: 'Mental distress'). Everything else is faithful: the high-risk rule's and/or mirrors the flowchart, the Urgent priority matches the box heading, and all concepts exist; minor points are the two 'Planning suicide' check_for entries that are indistinguishable to the health worker and the attempted branch not being given a risk diagnosis.
